page: Microsoft Azure M176-88bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBSMediumMemoryv3 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 88 dedicated vCPUs (44 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled) operating at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. It is equipped with 1536.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 17.45 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, but it is designed for high-performance block storage and is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multiple compute and memory subsystems. The server achieves top-tier status in Passmark CPU scores, Passmark database operations, and Passmark CPU extended instructions. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with large-block read-only operations reaching 420.52 GB/sec and write operations at 181.86 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% tier. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores are strong, placing in the top 25%. For specialized workloads, it demonstrates top-tier throughput in static web serving and strong performance in Redis SET operations. Large language model inference speeds are also strong, processing 253.91 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a medium 7B model.

Given its massive memory footprint and dedicated high-frequency Intel Xeon cores, the M176-88bs_v3 offers high resource density for memory-bound enterprise applications. The absence of local storage means storage costs are decoupled, allowing users to scale block storage independently. This hardware profile is highly suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory data stores like Redis, enterprise resource planning systems, and memory-intensive data analytics or simulation workloads.
